About
AfterHours

We make caffeine free energy for the part of the day that starts when the sun goes down.

Our story

Most energy drinks are built for 8 a.m. We built ours for 8 p.m.

Made for late hours

The shifts that run long, the deadlines that don’t care what time it is, the friends who are still up. AfterHours is for those hours.

Caffeine free, on purpose

We say it right on the can, directly under the logo. You shouldn’t have to read the fine print to find out what you’re drinking.

Named for the night sky

Dusky Peach, Midnight Cherry, Blackout Berry, Apple Eclipse, Moonrise Mango and Lunar Lemon Lime. Six flavors that run from dusk to dawn.

How it
works.

AfterHours has no caffeine. The lift comes from isomaltulose, a slow-digesting carbohydrate that releases energy gradually, and L-tyrosine, an amino acid linked to alertness and focus.

Monk fruit sweetens every flavor, and natural flavors give each can its taste.

  1. FormulateWe build each recipe with food chemists.
  2. TestEvery version gets tasted and checked.
  3. RefineWe adjust until the flavor and the lift are right.
  4. ApproveFinal sign-off, made with an FDA-registered co-packer.

A moon,
two sparks.

The AfterHours mark is a dark circle with a white crescent wrapped around it. “After” sits in the dark. “Hours” curves along the edge of the light.

Two small stars sit at the top, one for each end of the night. The can color changes with every flavor. The moon never does.

Read the FAQ

Questions,
answered.

The basics on what’s in the can, how long it lasts, and where to find it.

What does “caffeine free energy” mean?

AfterHours contains no caffeine. The lift comes from isomaltulose and L-tyrosine instead. Check the nutrition facts and ingredient list on the can for exactly what’s inside each flavor.

How does it work?

Isomaltulose is a slow-digesting carbohydrate that releases energy gradually. L-tyrosine is an amino acid linked to alertness and focus. Together they’re designed to give a smooth lift without the jitters.

How long does the lift last?

AfterHours is designed to give a lift of about 2–3 hours, then fade. There’s no caffeine, so there’s nothing left lingering for 10–12 hours.

What sweetens it?

Monk fruit, a natural sweetener from fruit. The flavors are natural, too.

Can I drink it at night?

That’s what it’s made for. There’s no caffeine, and the lift is designed to fade in 2–3 hours, so it fits the late hours. Everyone’s body is different, so go with what works for you.

What flavors are there?

Six: Dusky Peach, Midnight Cherry, Blackout Berry, Apple Eclipse, Moonrise Mango and Lunar Lemon Lime.

How big is a can, and what does it cost?

Every can is 12 fl oz (355 mL) and costs $2.50.

Who makes AfterHours?

Each flavor is formulated with food chemists, then tested, refined and approved before it ships. We work with an FDA-registered co-packer and ingredients backed by evidence.

Is it okay for everyone?

If you’re pregnant, nursing, under 18, or have a medical condition, talk to your doctor before trying any energy drink. If you have an allergy, read the ingredient list on the can first.

Where can I buy AfterHours?

We’re starting with campus exclusives, with more places on the way. A store finder is coming, so check back here soon.
